title: Peri Peri Chicken Platter
seoTitle: Peri Peri Chicken Platter | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Portuguese-African chili chicken with charred lemon for ten
subtitle: Portuguese-African chili chicken with charred lemon for ten
description: Chicken quarters marinate in peri peri chili sauce with lemon and garlic, then grill until charred and juicy. Serve on platters with grilled peppers, charred lemons, and extra sauce for dipping.

steps.title: Blend peri peri sauce
steps.instruction: Blend chilies, garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, paprika, oregano, and salt until smooth.

steps.title: Marinate chicken
steps.instruction: Coat quarters in half the sauce. Marinate at least 2 hours or overnight refrigerated.

steps.title: Preheat grill
steps.instruction: Heat grill to medium-high, about 400°F. Oil grates thoroughly. Target oven/smoker temperature: 400°F.

steps.title: Grill chicken and vegetables
steps.instruction: Grill chicken skin-side down 8 minutes, flip, and cook until 165°F internal, about 20 minutes total. Grill peppers, onions, and lemon halves alongside. Target oven/smoker temperature: 400°F.

steps.title: Platter and serve
steps.instruction: Rest chicken 5 minutes, then pile on platters with grilled vegetables. Drizzle reserved sauce and scatter cilantro.

proTips: Bird's eye chilies kick heat up—jalapeños keep it hall-friendly.
Peri peri mayo for dipping is an easy upgrade.
Portuguese rolls soak up sauce better than standard buns.
tonightSpread: Peri peri chicken with grilled peppers, onions, and charred lemon.
Simple rice or roasted potatoes for crew who want a plate, not just chicken.
leftovers: Pull meat for peri peri wraps with slaw—not a burrito bowl, a straight wrap.
Chop into grain salad with cucumber and feta.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Peri peri chicken brings real heat and tang—crews who live on hot sauce will line up twice. Quarters are cheap, grill fast, and look impressive piled on sheet pans.
mealPrepNotes: Marinate up to 24 hours. Reserve half the sauce for serving—never baste with used marinade from raw chicken. Spatchcock quarters if you need faster grill time.
